sentences.text: There's something disturbing about the way a crying angel clasps his hands in RAGE.
This is The Fallen Angel, painted by Alexandre Cabanel in 1847.
The angel lies on a rock ledge while distant angels fly above.
According to historical records, Cabanel painted this scene while staying at the Villa Medicis in Rome.
A fallen angel should show surrender.
But his hands remain locked in fury.
Tears run down his face, yet his hands stay clenched in anger.
As if his hands are preparing for a strike.
So is the angel weeping from sorrow, or locking his hands in rage?

meta.title: The Hidden Tension in Cabanel's Fallen Angel
meta.description: An examination of Alexandre Cabanel's 1847 painting The Fallen Angel. While tears fill Lucifer's eyes, his clasped hands show a deeper story.

sources.claim: The Fallen Angel (French: L'Ange déchu) is a painting by the French artist Alexandre Cabanel.
He lies on the ground, naked, while angels fly in the sky above to show the glory of God.
Analysis A Romantic work, the figure of Lucifer is shown as a nude, handsome young man reclining, hands clasped, his face partially obscured by his arm.
